# pytest-databricks-lakeflow

> A pytest plugin for testing the Lakeflow Jobs in a Databricks Asset Bundle. A test points at a job or a task in the bundle, the plugin deploys the bundle once per session, creates a throwaway copy of the job for the test, runs it with the chosen parameters, returns the per-task state, outputs, logs, printed notebook output, errors, task values and resolved parameters, and deletes the job. Task-level tests wrap one task with injected tasks that set upstream task values and capture the values it sets.

Install with `uv add --dev pytest-databricks-lakeflow` or `pip install pytest-databricks-lakeflow`. Requires Python 3.11 or later, the Databricks CLI v1.7.0 or later, and credentials for a workspace with serverless jobs. The public API is importable from `pytest_databricks_lakeflow`: `Lakeflow`, `EphemeralJob`, `JobRun`, `TaskRun`, `TaskValues`, `TaskError`, `Timing`, `NotebookView`, `NotebookCell`, `RunHandle`, `SqlResult`, `PipelineUpdate`, `LakeflowError`, `LakeflowBundleError`, `LakeflowTimeout`, `LakeflowRunFailed`, plus `serialise` from `pytest_databricks_lakeflow.results`. Tests get a `Lakeflow` from the session-scoped `lakeflow` fixture.

## Documentation

- [Home](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/): the README, with the pitch, a job test and a task test
- [Getting started](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/getting-started/): prerequisites, install, the bundle test target, configuring the fixture, the first test, CI
- [Writing job tests](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/job-tests/): lakeflow.job(), per-task parameter overrides (task_params=, merged or replaced by task type, warning when a job parameter wins), run(), stop_after for jobs that never end (a cancelled JobRun, JobRun.cancelled), start(timeout=) and RunHandle (wait, cancel, two jobs side by side), JobRun and TaskRun, if/else branches, retry attempts and timeouts, timing breakdown and effective performance target, resolved parameters, SQL, alert, dbt, run-job, dashboard and clean room task outputs and alert_state, SQL file task rows (TaskRun.sql_result, SqlResult), jobs that run other jobs (children="refuse", child_run_id, child_run), test-only dependencies (extra_dependencies, local wheels with extras such as ./dist/*.whl[test], modify_settings recipes for git_branch and libraries), per-job serverless environments (environments=), task timeouts and retries (task_overrides=, run(timeout=) and start(timeout=) lengthening the job timeout), raise_for_failure(), output_json, notebook cell output and stdout from jobs.export_run (TaskRun.notebook, notebook_export), only (a selected task that refers to the task values of a task left out raises LakeflowError), stubbing upstream tasks of a whole job (upstream_task_values=) and replaying a run's task values into them (run(only=..., replay=run)), pipeline refresh options (full_refresh, refresh_selection, refresh_flow_selection, reset_checkpoint_selection) and the update a pipeline task started (TaskRun.pipeline_update, PipelineUpdate.events), disable, force_conditions, capture_task_values, run_as, temporary schemas, setup= and teardown= functions, SQL statement lists (${name} placeholders) and .py notebook files that seed and clean up data on the job's compute, shared runs, keep rules, callbacks
- [Writing task tests](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/task-tests/): lakeflow.task(), stubs and probes, replaying a task from a previous run with upstream_from, setup= and teardown= before the stubs, value rules, helper compute, environments= for a serverless task's dependencies, task_params= and task_overrides= for the task under test
- [Configuration](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/configuration/): every Lakeflow argument, strict_artifacts for wheel artifacts without dynamic_version and, with sync="none", local wheels built after their uploaded copies, the test_marker job parameter that job code can read, bundle targets and variables, deploy flags, the CLI and SDK host check, permissions on ephemeral jobs, command-line flags, sweeping leftover jobs, schemas and setup/teardown notebooks (scope, branch, dry run, JSON report, keep TTL), environment variable and sync strategy, the --lakeflow-report-dir report directory (report.json per test, runs the plugin cancelled included, via serialise, raw logs, exported notebooks)
- [How it works](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/how-it-works/): session setup, isolating test deployments per branch and identity, the per-job lifecycle, teardown, xdist, what stays in the workspace, timing
- [Limitations and FAQ](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/limitations/)
- [API reference](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/api/): generated from the docstrings
- [Changelog](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/changelog/)
